subject.title: Feature request: config option to suppress transient tool error warnings

question: Should OpenClaw add a new normal-chat tool-error warning delivery policy beyond the existing `messages.suppressToolErrors` boolean, and what should the default safety behavior be when a mutating tool fails but the assistant final reply sounds successful?
rationale: The remaining work adds or redefines public config and intentionally changes user-visible safety semantics for failed side effects, so source inspection cannot choose the product contract safely.

options.title: Add explicit delivery policy
options.body: Design a public enum that preserves current safety by default while letting hosted or group-chat operators opt into final-only or off behavior with focused upgrade and channel tests.

options.title: Keep existing boolean only
options.body: Close or defer the enum request and document `messages.suppressToolErrors` as the operator-owned all-off mode.

options.title: Channel-specific policy
options.body: Push this into channel-owned configuration for Telegram, Discord, or other team-chat deployments instead of adding another global message config key.

recommendation.title: Add explicit delivery policy
recommendation.body: Design a public enum that preserves current safety by default while letting hosted or group-chat operators opt into final-only or off behavior with focused upgrade and channel tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent source blame and merged related warning-policy PRs point to this area for deciding the safety/default contract.
